label: original-phase input of 1/p/q/j/3/2/u after r/w/l/a-type tokens earlier in the sequence
explanation: Fires almost entirely in the original (input) phase (96% of mass), never at t=0, rarely at t=1, and peaks at t=2-4. It is weak and close to silent in the delimiter and copy phases (copy-phase activity is mostly at recall_idx 1). The current input token matters most: 1 alone holds 34% of mass (8.6x lift), then p, q, j, 3, 2 and u. Whether it fires on those tokens depends on what came earlier: the rate goes up when the prefix contains l, a, r, w (and z, x, e, o), e.g. first_tok r/w or prev/prev2 tok a/l. The strongest activations are 1 or p/q/j inputs after prefixes like r l l / w e l a / r l a. The predicate (key token in the input phase with >=2 such context tokens already seen) captures about two thirds of mass on dev but precision is only ~0.23. The neuron also fires weakly on many other tokens, and most key-token steps with the right context do not fire, so the dependence on hidden state is not fully captured by token-set rules. Inactive on <DEL> and on repeated (non-first) occurrences of a token in most cases.
